# An e2e exclusion cannot say its reason is real but incomplete, so a partial cause presents as a complete one

## Context

Split from `#18422` so that ticket can stay open on the divergence it has not explained, while the substrate work it produced lands. @neo-gpt's review of PR `#18423` caught that `Resolves #18422` would close a ticket both the ticket body and my own comment promise to keep open — the same conflict `#18408` resolved earlier tonight, in the same way.

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-09-07T00:58Z: `#18424`, `#18422`, `#18421`, `#18419`, `#18414`, `#18410` — no equivalent.

## The Problem

`buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` declares why each e2e spec is outside the CI tier, and the job summary prints those reasons on every run. Its `kind` field had two values:

- `cause` — we know why
- `observed` — we do not

Both honest, and between them they cannot express the case that actually occurs: **a reason that is real and incomplete.**

`LivePreviewMultiWindow` was marked `cause` with *"the Dist environments need built bundles this job does not produce"*. True, and it covers 8 of 11 failing arms. The other 3 are the **Dev** environment, which needs no build at all — they fail hosted while all 4 pass locally in 40.2s:

```
PASS  32  Dev - Popout LivePreview from Home Route (Helix)     8.4s
FAIL  33  Dev - Popout LivePreview from Learn Route           30.6s
FAIL  34  Dev - Sequential Route: Home -> Learn -> Popout     41.7s
FAIL  35  Dev - Sequential Route: Learn -> Home -> Popout     30.7s
```

So the entry's owner field promised a remedy — *"the day the pipeline can afford a build step"* — that would not have worked. Whoever took that lane would have built the bundles and found three arms still red.

A partial explanation presenting as a complete one is the same false reassurance an undeclared exclusion gives, wearing better clothes. The file exists to prevent exactly that, and could not detect it in itself.

## The Fix

A third `kind`, `partial`, rendered as **"cause covers only part of the failures"**, with an owner field that can split between the explained and unexplained halves.

And the same discipline applied to the entry being diagnosed: a detailed measurement of *what* happens is not a *cause*, so it is classified `observed` even though its reason is the richest in the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An exclusion can declare a reason that is real but does not cover every failing arm in its file, and the job summary says so.
- [ ] The partial entry names the surface its reason does not explain, not merely that one exists.
- [ ] An entry whose measurement establishes a behaviour rather than a cause is classified `observed`.
- [ ] Every exclusion's owner field is answerable: no owner is promised a remedy that would not work.
- [ ] The selection floor still passes with the classifications changed.

## Out of Scope

- Why the portal diverges on a hosted runner — that is `#18422`, and it stays open.
- The three unexplained `LivePreview` Dev arms, which are recorded under my ownership in the standing exclusion.
- Any Portal repair.

## Related

- `#18422` — the measurement that exposed this, staying open on the unexplained divergence.
- `#18408` — the tier whose exclusion declarations this improves.

* test(portal): the learn-link arm returns to CI with a timeout sized by the hosted trace (#18422)

The arm was excluded from the e2e tier as an observed failure with no established cause,
and I owned it — deliberately, after guessing "needs generated learn content" and being
shown the guide and the learn index are both tracked. This replaces the guess with a
measurement.

Local instruments could not see it. The arm passes in isolation (4 passed, 6.3s) and at
the same serial position inside the full tier (test 30 of 37, 807ms), so it is not serial
position, state accumulation or resource pressure.

The hosted failure artifact carries the answer. The click is not the problem: the
selector resolved, Playwright logged `navigations have finished`, and the trace holds no
console error and no failed request. The frame snapshots settle it:

    140971.2  …index.html#/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts
    141020.8  …index.html#/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption   ← routed
    146050.4  …index.html#/learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption   ← 5s later

The route changed and the content did not follow within the default 5s window, while the
sibling sidebar arm passed on the same runner.

What is NOT established is whether the content arrives later or never, and the trace ends
at the timeout so it cannot say. 30s distinguishes the two, and the hosted run this
change enables is the discriminator: green means the default window was too tight for a
hosted runner, red means the content genuinely never follows and the target is far
narrower than "fails on a hosted runner".

The exclusion is therefore removed and the spec returned to the tier — a measurement is
worth more than a permanent exclusion carrying an admission that nobody knows why.

Verified by removing the production `rewriteLinks` invocation: arms 1, 2 and 4 red while
the sidebar control stays green, which is what the spec's docblock predicts and what
keeps the wider timeout from turning it into a witness of nothing.

* test(portal): the learn-link exclusion states a measured cause instead of an unknown (#18422)

The hosted run this branch enabled was the experiment, and it falsified the hypothesis
the previous commit was built on. Recording the result rather than the guess.

Widening the destination assertion to 30s and running it hosted changed nothing: the arm
still failed, at 32.4s. So the divergence is NOT a timing budget, and the earlier commit's
timeout is reverted — a longer window buys a slower failure and nothing else.

What the trace and that run together establish:

  the click resolves its anchor, Playwright logs `navigations have finished`,
  the hash arrives at the destination, and the source `h1` is still in place
  30 seconds later, with no console error and no failed request

The route changes. The content never follows. The sibling sidebar arm passes on the same
runner, so the content component can update there; it is the route-driven update after an
in-content link that does not.

The spec is therefore correct and stays excluded, but its entry is now `kind: 'cause'`
with that measurement instead of an admission that nobody knew why. The tier's exclusion
list carries no `cause not established` entries any more — both remaining exclusions state
what was measured and who holds them.

Two things this deliberately does not claim: why a hosted Ubuntu runner diverges from a
local macOS one, and whether any user-facing path is affected. Neither is established, and
the arm is a witness rather than a repair.

* ci(test): an exclusion can now say its cause covers only part of the failures (#18422)

I claimed in this PR that the tier's exclusion list carried no unexplained entry. That
was wrong, and the wrongness was mine from the start.

The LivePreview exclusion reads "the Dist environments need built bundles this job does
not produce". True, and it covers 8 of 11 failing arms. It does not cover the other 3:
those are the DEV environment, which needs no build at all, and they failed on the same
hosted run while all 4 Dev arms pass locally in 40.2s.

So a build step — the remedy the owner field promised — would not have returned this file
to the tier, and anyone reading the entry would have believed it would.

`kind` gains a third value. `cause` and `observed` split "we know why" from "we do not",
and both were honest; what neither could express is a reason that is real and incomplete.
An entry marked `cause` was quietly asserting its explanation covered EVERY failing arm in
that file, and the summary now says so out loud when it does not.

The owner field splits with it: this tier still holds the Dist half, and I hold the 3 Dev
arms, which have no explanation yet.

Deliberately not claimed: the 3 Dev failures all involve the portal's Learn route, and the
one Dev arm that passes is Home-only — while the other portal spec in this tier also fails
hosted on a learn navigation. That is a suggestive coincidence, not a shared cause, and
tonight already produced one four-arm shared-cause story that a bisect killed.

* ci(test): the partial cause names the surface it does not cover (#18422)

Checking whether the three unexplained Dev arms share a cause with the other portal
exclusion, rather than assuming it from the pattern. They do not, and the entry now says
what they actually fail on.

All three die on `.neo-code-live-preview` never becoming visible, and all three are the
arms that visit `#/learn/benefits/body/FormsEngine`. The one Dev arm that never leaves
the home route passes on the same run.

That looked like kinship with the other portal exclusion, where a route change leaves the
content behind — same app, same hosted-only shape, both touching learn routes. It is not.
`LearnLinkRoutingNL`'s first two arms go straight to a learn guide and PASS hosted,
finding anchors inside the rendered prose, so a learn guide's content renders there. What
does not render is a live-preview component inside one, while the same component on the
home route does.

Two hosted-only portal failures on different surfaces. Writing them up as one cause would
have handed whoever takes them a single hunt for something that is not there — which is
the story a bisect had to kill once already tonight.

* ci(test): the learn-link entry says observed, because a behaviour is not a cause (#18422)

@neo-gpt's review. I marked it `kind: 'cause'` on the strength of a detailed measurement,
but what the measurement establishes is WHAT happens — the click routes, the hash lands,
the content never follows, at 5s and at 30s, with no error. It does not establish WHY a
hosted Ubuntu runner diverges from a local macOS one.

That is the same overclaim I added `partial` to stop on the entry directly beside it: a
real, specific, well-evidenced reason presenting as a complete explanation. Having built
the guard, I walked into its neighbouring case one commit later.

`observed` keeps the label honest and loses nothing — the reason field still carries every
measurement, and the summary now prints `cause not established` above it, which is exactly
true.
